title: He couldn't remember practising, yet he improved

probes.question: True or false: H.M. improved at mirror drawing even though he had no memory of the previous attempts.
What was the mirror drawing task?
options: Tracing a star while looking at a reflection

image.alt: Illustration of a pencil tracing a star between two close outlines, seen as if in a mirror

panels.text: Henry Molaison, known as H.M., had parts of his brain removed in 1953 in an attempt to cure his epilepsy.
Afterwards he developed severe anterograde amnesia: he lost his ability to remember.
In the early 1960s, Brenda Milner asked him to trace a star while only looking at a reflection of his paper and pencil in a mirror. At first he went outside the lines about 30 times.
By the tenth trial on the first day he only made about 5-6 errors, even though he had no memory of the previous attempts.
